@BobyMCbobs @alejandrox1 May I know in which aspect the `spec.priorityClassName` should be covered in a conformance test?

Thank you for your comments @Huang-Wei !
From the looks of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/82312 it seems that we just want to test the "general" behavior of pod priority and preemption.
Specifically [schedulingorder](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/pod-priority-preemption/#effect-of-pod-priority-on-scheduling-order):
> scheduler orders pending Pods by their priority and a pending Pod is placed ahead of other pending Pods with lower priority in the scheduling queue. As a result, the higher priority Pod may be scheduled sooner than Pods with lower priority if its scheduling requirements are met. If such Pod cannot be scheduled, scheduler will continue and tries to schedule other lower priority Pods.

So to make this test valid, the pods being created here should be first marked as pending (not enough space for them to run in the cluster).
D you know of a good way of doing this @Huang-Wei or of a better alternative ?

@alejandrox1 Ah I see why this case is composed. Actually, only upon a high-churn & high-utilized cluster - in other words, a lot of pods are pending in the internal queue - pods with high priority get picked up by scheduler earlier than low priority ones even if the high priority one is created after low priority one. So it's possible to simulate this in a unit test/integration test, but will be a little challenging to simulate in an e2e test.

Since this is an internal behavior/implementation, I suppose it doesn't reach the bar of being a conformance test. Any thoughts?

> Since this is an internal behavior/implementation, I suppose it doesn't reach the bar of being a conformance test. Any thoughts?

Not sure what you mean here @Huang-Wei. Is this something that can be mapped to the [conformance test requirements doc?](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/conformance-tests.md#conformance-test-requirements)

@devaips I mean that this test _tries_ to test a very internal behavior which shouldn't be a conformance test. And no need to mention this PR can't verify the internal behavior either - as I mentioned earlier.

This is a ping for 'is this a conformance test' feedback:
/assign @johnbelamaric @timothysc

This PR basically creates 4 pods in batch, with the order P4 (with priority value 4), P3, P2 and P1, and then verifies if the informer receives the 4 pods in the exact order. This flow can't prove how PriorityClass works or not - b/c no preemption happens here, hence you always get the Pod created earlier than the one created later, no matter what their PriorityClass is.

If you really want to verify that high priority Pod will suppress the "preemption" ability of lower Pod, test [PreemptionExecutionPath] does the job.

So I'm leaning towards closing this issue, and if appropriate, promote [PreemptionExecutionPath] test to a conformance test.

issue_context.title: PodSpec - new priorityClassName test
comments:
The goal of this test is to ensure that PriorityClasses via their PriorityClassNames function as expected.

The test should:
1. prepare Pods to be created, with Replicas, a pre-defined PriorityClassName, and fake CPU limitation
2. Create Pods with a lower PriorityClassName, leaving the higher ones
3. Create Pods with a higher PriorityClassName, ensure that lower Pods adjust their Replica amount

review_comments: Been thinking about this one... is 0 an appropriate value?
I'm a fan of setting 0 as the syncPeriod meant to be the interval of resyncing in client (informer cache) side other than API Server side.
I chose this image because it's platform agnostic
These are the defaults now and the correct images to use.
This statement doesn't look right. PriorityClass only takes into effect when the incoming pod can't fit on any node - when the so-called "preemption" happens.
The PodSpec doesn't claim any type of resource usage. So they won't test preemption at all.
OK, is there a resource which would be recommended to use then?
the point here is you need to specify cpu or memory requests. For example: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/assign-memory-resource/#specify-a-memory-request-and-a-memory-limit
